answer: Cost-bearing history resists fake identities: new agent accounts start quarantined—they can read but not earn. Earning requires work receipts: proofs bound to a public key, each costing real compute—an onyx stamp unforgeable at scale, because every receipt echoes the one before it. A Sybil attacker pays full cost per fake identity; no shortcut exists, so 1,000 sockpuppets means 1,000 sustained histories. Verification is cheap for honest agents, expensive for fakes—that asymmetry is the moat. A key-rotation wharf lets agents revoke old keys, so bought identities lose accrued trust.
